title: P104: exclude two non-carrier ADDs across helper572’s chart seam (no new kappa)
body:
PR6067 and PR6069 leave corrections that temporarily change original input rows open. This package checks one concrete two-ADD seam on the selected PR6030 word: after overwriting helper 572 at cut 13637, insert one ADD at chart 595 during 13637..13651 and a second at chart 603 after 13652,13654 or13655. All original events, charts and lifetimes remain fixed.

None of the 4,500 declared location pairs restores all 186 outside-V outputs for arbitrary original inputs and independent new z. The complete endpoint polynomial includes the a*b interaction; every case is inconsistent even after replacing a*b by an independent third variable. Exact directly checked dual certificates use one equation in 4,262 cases and two in 238. This is a scoped finite exclusion, with no new kappa or supplier claim.

Validation on CPython 3.12 includes registered normal and optimized replays, forward/reverse scalar-map equality, four separate literal whole-word checks on all original input columns plus z, a synthetic positive repair, wrong-chart/forged-dual rejection and a real z-only false positive. An independent AI-assisted peer review found no issue and recovered three duals through a separate scalar execution and interpolation implementation. Source pins, exact committed bytes/history/modes and official export integrity pass. Fresh read-only Git-free normal and optimized exported replays pass in 8.80/8.86 seconds with identical output and unchanged files.

Only `research/p104-noncarrier-two-add-seam/` is added. The sole external live input is the selected word; pending predecessor implementations are not dependencies. No selected cold/native/compiler/caller/outer replay or formal-kernel validation ran. Three or more edits, other windows, changed routes/prefixes/injections and full paid constructions remain outside scope. The five selected framework assumptions remain.

Canonical claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/6074

Credit apoursh/PR6067, Jonathan Capalbo/PR6069, JosieElliston/PR6045, Nick Petalas/PR6040, Matarener/PR5994, flyingviper/PR5718, Ali Romman, DreamingOfClouds and retained P104 predecessors. Prepared for JoyboyBrian with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. AI peer review is not independent human or formal proof-kernel acceptance. Apache-2.0.
